name: HDMI Type-A (19-pin)
description: The standard 19-pin HDMI connector. The bulk of the pins carry three TMDS differential data pairs plus a TMDS clock pair (each pair is +, shield, -). The rest are control: CEC (device control), the DDC I2C bus (SCL/SDA, for EDID), a utility/ARC/eARC line, +5V, and Hot Plug Detect. Odd pins sit on one row, even on the other (staggered).

contacts.name: +5V
contacts.description: +5 V power (up to 50 mA, for the sink's EDID EEPROM etc.)

variants: Same 19 signals appear on Mini-HDMI (Type-C) and Micro-HDMI (Type-D) in different physical pin orders -- the pinout numbers differ per connector, only the signal set is shared.
ARC / eARC reuse pins 14 and 19 (the HEAC pair) to send audio back from a TV to a soundbar; older cables that leave those unconnected won't pass ARC.
gotchas: The three TMDS data pairs + clock pair are high-speed differential lines -- impedance-controlled, length-matched. This is not something to hand-wire; a bad joint gives sparkles or a black screen, not a graceful degrade.
DDC (pins 15/16) is a plain I2C bus the source uses to read the display's EDID. A flaky DDC line = 'no signal' or wrong resolution even when the video pairs are fine.
Pin 18 supplies only ~50 mA at 5 V -- it powers the sink's EDID EEPROM and HPD, not a device. Don't try to run anything real off it.
Hot Plug Detect (pin 19) is how the source knows a display is connected; if HPD is low the source may never output video even with a good cable.
notes: HDMI Type-A 19-pin pinout cross-checked against Wikipedia's HDMI connector table. Odd/even staggered rows.
